detail.longDescription: Consider the following examples of URLs: URL Root https://fr-wiktionary-org.translate.goog/wiki/s translate.goog https://python.regex.parse.smackoverflow.net/questions/answer smackoverflow.net www.linkedout.com/out/jane-doe linkedout.com http://www.linkedout.com/out/jane-doe linkedout.com https://www.linkedout.com/out/jane-doe linkedout.com The root of a URL is always of the form something.something . The root contains the right-most dot ( . ) that is to the left of the forward slashes ( / ), except for the forward slashes ( / ) inside of https:// . What Python regular expression will place the root of a URL inside of a capturing group, and discard the other parts of the URL? The following regex almost works: (?:https?:\/\/)??(?:[0-9a-zA-Z-\.])*\.([0-9a-zA-Z-]+\.[0-9a-zA-Z-]+){1}(?:[0-9a-zA-Z-\/]*) Regex101 If the capturing group for root of the URL is lazy instead of greedy, then we have bad results for the root capturing group, such as e.g , instead of translate.goog . The root of a URL is similar to, but not the same as, the longest possible sub-string of the URL that includes exactly one dot . (not two dots, or three dots, etc.) and such that our sub-string of interest does not contain any forward slashes / .
